title: Semantic Versioning Discipline
description: Semver encodes compatibility in the version number: major for breaking, minor for additive, patch for fixes. Clients can trust the numbers only if the discipline is real. The practice is simple; the enforcement is the work.

title: Breaking Change Detection
description: API diffs compare the old and new schema to flag breaking changes automatically: removed fields, narrowed types, new required parameters. CI fails the build on unexpected breaks. Detection turns discipline into automation.

title: Consumer-Driven Contract Testing
description: Consumers publish their expectations as contracts, and providers verify against them. Pact is the canonical tool. The provider knows exactly what it must not break because the consumers said so.

demo.code:
pact = {"consumer": "web", "expects": {"GET /user": 200}}
print("pact:", pact)
print("provider verifies: GET /user returns 200 -> PASS")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Pact', 'contract': 'Consumer expectations', 'method': 'Provider verification', 'check': 'All pacts green', 'benefit': 'Know what not to break', 'complexity': 'Medium'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'contract', 'method', 'check', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: API Evolution with Field Addition
description: Adding optional fields is the safest evolution: old clients ignore them, new clients use them. The rule is additive-only within a major version. Evolution without breakage is a design choice.

title: Deprecation Sunset Process
description: Deprecations follow a process: announce, warn in responses, then remove after the sunset period. Headers carry the sunset date. The process respects the clients' upgrade time.

demo.code:
print("Sunset: Sat, 01 Jan 2027")
print("Deprecation: true, Link: <docs>; rel=successor")
print("remove only after sunset date")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Sunset headers', 'contract': 'Deprecation policy', 'method': 'Announce-warn-remove', 'check': 'Sunset honored', 'benefit': 'Respectful removal', 'complexity': 'Low'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'contract', 'method', 'check', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Backward Compatibility Test Suite
description: A suite of old-client tests runs against every new server build, proving compatibility empirically. The tests encode the compatibility promise. Green means the promise holds.

demo.code:
tests = ["v1_login", "v1_search", "v2_login"]
results = {t: "PASS" for t in tests}
print(results)
print("promise holds:", all(v == "PASS" for v in results.values()))

title: Schema Registry Governance
description: A schema registry versions every API schema and rejects incompatible changes per the configured policy. Producers and consumers coordinate through the registry. Governance is centralized and automatic.

demo.code:

print("register v4: BREAKING -> REJECTED (policy)")

assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'contract', 'method', 'check', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())

title: Tolerant Reader Pattern
description: Clients read only the fields they need and ignore the rest, tolerating server evolution. The pattern decouples client and server release cycles. Robustness comes from ignoring, not from knowing.

title: API Linting for Compatibility
description: Linters check API definitions against compatibility rules before they merge: no removed enums, no new required fields. The rules encode hard-won experience. Linting catches what review misses.

demo.code:
rules = ["no-removed-enum", "no-new-required"]
violations = []
print("rules:", rules)
print("violations:", violations or "none -> merge allowed")

title: Version Negotiation
description: Client and server negotiate the highest mutually supported version at handshake. Both sides implement version ranges. Negotiation lets old and new coexist gracefully.

demo.code:
client, server = [1, 2, 3], [2, 3, 4]
common = max(set(client) & set(server))
print("client:", client, "server:", server)
print("negotiated:", common)

title: Expandable Enums
description: Enums are designed expandable: unknown values are preserved and passed through, never rejected. Clients handle the unknown case explicitly. The API can grow its vocabulary without breaking readers.

demo.code:
known = {"red", "blue"}
value = "green"
print("received:", value)
print("action:", "preserve and pass through" if value not in known else "handle")

title: Contract-First Design
description: The contract is written before the implementation, reviewed, and then both sides build to it. Design discussions happen in the contract, not in code. First means first.

demo.code:

print("2. review with consumers")
print("3. implement to the contract")

print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Parallel Version Serving
description: Multiple API versions serve simultaneously behind versioned routes, letting clients migrate at their pace. Old versions get security fixes but no features. Parallel serving buys migration time.

title: Change Data Capture for APIs
description: API changes are published as events so consumers learn about deprecations programmatically. The changelog is machine-readable. Consumers adapt automatically where possible.

title: Compatibility Matrix Testing
description: Every client version is tested against every server version in a matrix, proving the full compatibility story. The matrix is the contract made executable. Gaps in the matrix are risks made visible.

title: Graceful Degradation Contracts
description: The contract states what happens when a field is missing: defaults, not errors. Servers degrade gracefully for old clients. The contract documents the degradation, so it's designed, not accidental.

demo.code:

email = payload.get("email", "none@example.com")
print("missing email -> default:", email)
